contract: construct() -> list of distinct integers in [0, n] forming an admissible tuple: for every prime p <= len(tuple) some residue class mod p is missed (FunSearch fixed-diameter formulation). Score: tuple size
notes: The source itself uses a fixed diameter bound n=5000 and maximizes surviving tuple size. The local constructor directly returns integers in[0,5000]; for k distinct values it checks a missing residue for every prime<=k (larger primes cannot be fully occupied). The source instead evolves a prime-residue sieve priority. The mathematical feasible set/size objective are shared but candidate interface and search differ. MCTS-AHD ternary admissible sets are a different task and have been restored separately.

name: Narrow admissible tuple
description: Construct the largest admissible tuple within [0, 5000] by selecting a removed residue class for each prime. This is the fixed-diameter maximization formulation actually benchmarked in paper Table 2.
limitations: Execution interface inspected in pinned source. Full paper experiments have not been reproduced here.
